name: Magadha (Nanda Empire)

areaKm2.note: The world_bc323 Magadha polygon measures 1.276 million km2 (the pipeline area function). It runs from the eastern Punjab to Bengal and Odisha, the "Punjab to Odisha" extent Bronkhorst (2011) gives on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanda_Empire. Low drops the uncertain margins (Kalinga, the Vindhyan forest belt), a judgement; high rounds up. For scale, Taagepera (1979) gives Magadha 0.5 million km2 in 510 BCE, before the Nanda expansion (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_largest_empires).

population.note: Dyson (2018) via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maurya_Empire: South Asia held 15-30 million in the Mauryan period. The Nanda share (Ganges plain, Bengal, Odisha, eastern Malwa) is taken as 40-60%, a judgement from the plain being the densest farmland of the subcontinent: 0.4 x 15M = 6M (low), 0.45 x 22.5M = 10M (mid), 0.6 x 30M = 18M (high). No modern estimate for the Nanda realm itself was found; the page gives none. The superseded phase-3 formula gave 9.6-24.7M for the same polygon.

urbanization.note: Educated guess. Pataliputra, Rajagriha, Varanasi, Kaushambi, Shravasti and Champa (the second urbanisation of the Ganges valley); overwhelmingly rural. The Maurya snapshot uses 0.07.

activePersonnel.note: Educated guess. Sum of the force guesses plus crews. Curtius' report to Alexander: 200,000 infantry, 20,000 cavalry, 2,000 four-horse chariots and 3,000 elephants (Habib and Jha 2004, Singh 2008, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanda_Empire); Diodorus 4,000 elephants (Raychaudhuri 1988, same page); Plutarch's 80,000 cavalry, 8,000 chariots and 6,000 elephants are called inflated there. Worthington (2014, same page) suggests Indian informants exaggerated to deter the Macedonians, so the Curtius totals with crews are the high bound, not the mid; mid ~1.25% of the 10M population, near the 1% of the Maurya snapshot.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Guild (sreni), allied and forest-tribe levies reachable within a month, as for the Maurya snapshot.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Mahouts and crews for ~2,000 elephants (2 each), drivers and fighters of ~1,000 chariots, commissariat and river transport.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess. Salaried standing army plus levies, as in the Maurya snapshot two generations later; a few percent of an agrarian population.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Educated guess. Spear and shield infantry of the standing army; Curtius gives 200,000 infantry in all (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanda_Empire), shared here among line, archers and light troops at the high end.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5 (era-typical). Evidence: iron spears and swords, little body armour, as Greek writers describe Indian infantry

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: a paid royal army existed (the dynasty is called militaristic on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanda_Empire), but no drill tradition is recorded

count.note: Educated guess. Archers with the long bamboo bow described by Megasthenes and Arrian (as in the Maurya snapshot); share of the Curtius infantry total.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: powerful but slow long bow

count.note: Educated guess. Javelin men and forest-tribe skirmishers in pay.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: light weapons

count.note: Educated guess. Horsemen; Curtius 20,000 (high). Indian cavalry was light and secondary to elephants.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5 minus. Evidence: small horses, no stirrups

count.note: Educated guess. Platform count. Curtius 2,000 four-horse chariots (high, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanda_Empire); chariots were declining in Indian warfare.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: heavy four-horse chariots, a generation behind

count.note: Educated guess. Platform count. Curtius 3,000, Diodorus 4,000 (high), both on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanda_Empire; the largest elephant corps of the age, later inherited by the Mauryas.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75 (among the era best). Evidence: the elephant corps that made Alexander's army refuse to cross the Beas

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: royal elephant establishment

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.5. Evidence: no Nanda battle record survives; the dynasty fell to Chandragupta and Chanakya within about four years (c. 322 BCE), the Milinda Panha recalling a violent war against the general Bhaddasala (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanda_Empire)

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.25-0.5. Evidence: an unpopular dynasty accused of greed and oppressive taxation in the Sri Lankan tradition (Habib and Jha 2004 via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanda_Empire), and a mix of standing troops and levies

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.5 (average). Evidence: no war in progress on home soil; Porus described the king as of "worthless character" (Diodorus, same page)

weapons.note: Anchor 3 (300 BCE iron weapons) minus. Evidence: iron swords and spears, the long bow; no torsion artillery attested.

armor.note: Anchor between 2 (bronze scale) and 3. Evidence: Greek sources describe lightly armoured Indian troops.

ships.note: Anchor between 2 and 3. Evidence: river craft on the Ganges and coastal boats from Tamralipti.

fortification.note: Anchor 3 minus. Evidence: the cyclopean wall of Rajagriha and the timber palisade of Pataliputra (64 gates and 570 towers by the Maurya period, Megasthenes via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maurya_Empire).

logistics.note: Anchor 3 minus. Evidence: the Uttarapatha trunk road and river transport; Jayaswal reads the Hathigumpha inscription as crediting a Nandaraja with a canal (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanda_Empire).

communications.note: Anchor between 2 (couriers) and 3. Evidence: royal couriers; no relay system recorded before the Mauryas.

isr.note: Anchor between 2 and 3. Evidence: scouts and spies; the Arthashastra spy system is Mauryan.

gdpPerCapita.note: Analogue as in maurya--250: Maddison 2023 (via OWID grapher CSV, https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/gdp-per-capita-maddison-project-database.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true) has no India value before 1600; its year-1 values are Egypt 1,116, Iran 1,116, Belgium/France 956 (2011 int$). Ganges Magadha placed in that band.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. A large standing army and elephant corps paid from land revenue; the tradition of a vast Nanda treasury (80 koti in the Mahavamsa, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanda_Empire) suggests heavy taxation. No budget survives.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Iron working, punch-marked silver coinage, crafts in a mostly agrarian economy.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Fertile Ganges plain with rice cultivation; as the Maurya snapshot.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in a pre-modern age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model as the classical and medieval snapshots.

roadKm.note: Educated guess. The Uttarapatha along the Ganges and the routes to Avanti; no engineered network.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. Tamralipti on the Bay of Bengal and the river ports of the Ganges.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. River and coastal craft; no figures.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Ox-cart and elephant trains inside the river and road network, a little below the Maurya snapshot.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Oxen, buffalo and some horses; about 0.25 per inhabitant, the Maurya snapshot ratio.

homeDefense.note: 1.1 (familiar terrain, local supply) to 1.2 (fortified Pataliputra and Rajagriha); the monsoon and river crossings hamper invaders.

notes: Snapshot = summer 326 BCE, the last Nanda king (Dhana Nanda, the Agrammes or Xandrames of the Greeks) when Alexander's army refused to cross the Beas; Chandragupta Maurya overthrew the dynasty c. 322 BCE. Every army figure is an ancient report (Curtius, Diodorus, Plutarch) of what Indian informants told the Macedonians; they only bound the high side. Population is the weakest number: Dyson's range for all of South Asia times a judged share. Border: world_bc323 Magadha is the file at the snapshot date. Population convention: everything inside the polygon; Porus and the Punjab kingdoms are excluded. Elephants and chariots are platforms; mahouts and crews are in supportPersonnel. Personnel: active = standing royal troops with the elephants and chariots; trainedReserves = guild, allied and forest-tribe levies.
